Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the respondents.

2. Petitioner is aggrieved by the award passed by the Arbitrator in terms of National Highway Act,
1956.
It is the case of the petitioner that his lands were acquired and award has been passed wherein a meager amount of compensation has been fixed.
Section 3-G(6) of the National Highway Act, 1956 deals with determination of the amount payable as compensation.

Section 3-G(5) reads as follows: -
3-G. Determination of amount payable as compensation.-
(1)... (2)... (3)... (4) ...
(5) If the amount determined by the competent authority under sub-section (1) or sub-section(2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an Sharda Mahesh Pratap Deo Son Of Late ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71886607/
1 application by either of the parties, be determined by the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government.

sentences.text: 3. Admittedly, an award has been passed by the Arbitrator appointed by the Central Government and an amount has been fixed.
If the petitioner is aggrieved by the award, remedy lies in terms of Section 3-G(6) of the National Highway Act, 1956.

As the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act is made applicable by the said section, appropriate forum available to the petitioner is to challenge the award in terms of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
4. Since there is an alternative remedy, the only remedy before the petitioner is in terms of Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

Thus, this writ petition is not maintainable and is,
accordingly, dismissed.

Pending interlocutory applications, if any, stand disposed of.
